title: Graph skills
examples: How do I know which graph to use for this data?
What does it mean when a graph shows a trend?
Can you show me an example of describing a trend?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to read different kinds of graphs. You will learn to choose the right graph for your data. This helps us show patterns in the world.
If you are comparing amounts between different groups, use a bar graph. For example, you could compare the population of three cities.
If you are showing how one thing changes over time, use a line graph. For instance, you could track the average temperature across a year.
To show parts of a whole, like how people travel, use a pie chart. For example, you could show the percentage of students who walk or cycle to school.

draw.text: Pie Chart: Parts of a whole

explain.say: When describing a trend, look for patterns in the data. You might say the trend is increasing, decreasing, or staying stable.
In real life, a line graph is perfect for tracking pollution levels in a river over many years. It clearly shows if the levels are getting better or worse.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bar graph and a line graph?
faq.a: A bar graph compares separate amounts at specific points. A line graph shows how something changes continuously over time.
asks: When should I use bars versus lines?
Do I use bars for time periods?

faq.q: How do I know if a trend is increasing or decreasing?
faq.a: If the line goes up from left to right, the trend is increasing. If the line goes down, the trend is decreasing.
asks: What does a rising trend look like?
How do I spot a falling trend?

faq.q: Can I use a pie chart for anything other than percentages?
faq.a: No, a pie chart must show parts that add up to a whole, which is usually represented by one hundred percent.
asks: Is a pie chart for counts?
Does the whole have to be 100?

faq.q: What is the best graph for showing two related measurements?
faq.a: A scatter graph is often best for showing the relationship between two different sets of numbers, like height and weight.
asks: How do I show two variables?

faq.q: If the line graph is flat, what does that mean about the data?
faq.a: A flat line means the value is staying the same or constant over that period of time.
asks: What does a horizontal line mean?
Is a flat line good or bad?

facts: Line graphs show continuous change over time.
Pie charts must represent parts of a whole.
A trend can be increasing, decreasing, or stable.

quiz.say: You want to compare the number of students who prefer apples, bananas, and grapes. Which graph should you use?
quiz.why: Bar graphs are best for comparing separate, distinct amounts.

wrong.0: A line graph implies that the categories are connected in a sequence.
wrong.1: A pie chart requires that the categories add up to a total whole.
wrong.2: A scatter graph shows relationships between two different types of numbers.

quiz.say: A graph shows that the amount of rainfall was 10 millimeters in May and 30 millimeters in June. What is the trend?
quiz.why: Since the value went up from 10 to 30, the trend is increasing.

wrong.0: Decreasing means the number would have to go down from May to June.
wrong.1: Stable means the amount would have to stay at 10 millimeters.
wrong.2: Fluctuating suggests the value went up and then down, which did not happen here.

quiz.say: Which graph type is best for showing what percentage of a school's students use different modes of transport?
quiz.why: A pie chart is designed to show how different parts make up one complete whole.

wrong.0: A line graph is used for measuring change over time, not parts of a total.
wrong.1: A scatter graph compares two different measured variables, not parts of one total.
wrong.3: While possible, a bar graph does not visually emphasize that the parts sum to one whole.
